Issued at 420 PM EDT Thu May 21 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Upper low swirling over MT this morning and digging into the 
Intermountain West, amid broad troughing across the western 
US...ahead of upstream ridging off the PacNW. Subtle upper ridging 
across the MS Valley into the Appalachians...with northern stream 
troughing slipping through eastern Canada with a 120+kt upper jet 
near ME. Bulk of the moisture is beneath this ridging thanks to deep 
return flow off the Gulf...from the central/southern Plains through 
the OH Valley and Mid-Atlantic, where pwats reach or exceed 1.5in. 
However, there is a bit of an uptick in moisture across the northern 
Plains ahead of aforementioned upper low...with strong southerly 
flow (around 30kts) from the central into the northern Plains, ahead 
of a surface boundary stretching from southeast Saskatchewan to CO 
and back into the Intermountain West with that upper low. Surface 
high pressure centered over eastern Lake Superior this morning with 
very dry air present here through much of the column (pwat of 0.21in 
on this morning's sounding is near the climo minimum). 

High pressure to slowly exit stage right tonight...as some of the PV 
currently over the Intermountain West digs across the northern 
Plains Friday. Currently expecting this to develop surface troughing 
across the Mid-MS and OH Valleys...leaving the Upper Great Lakes in 
strengthening easterly return flow between this and the departing 
high. Upper low will only slowly meander eastward over southern 
Canada...and potential niblets in the flow will dictate how 
rainy/organized this weekend's weather will be...but appears the 
primary trough axis should swing through Sunday/Sunday 
night...allowing upstream ridging to build across the central US. 
Will again need to keep an eye on potential activity to track 
through the flow into our area early next week...but signals point 
toward increasingly warm conditions overall as we wrap up the month 
of May...with potential for an Omega block to set up in the northern 
stream of the flow, which could be centered in the vicinity of the 
Midwest/Great Lakes by late next week. Stay tuned. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Frost Tonight...Anomalously dry air mass in place across the area 
today...with dewpoints thus far this afternoon in the mid-upper 20s 
to lower 30s. Lack of diurnal cu development through 17z further 
suggests the low levels are quite dry, even with some mid-level 
(10kft+) moisture sneaking in from the west ahead of a couple subtle 
niblets that should track through the area this evening...and think 
the mid-level cloud cover is all we'll be able to get from this. 
This could limit the amount of radiational cooling we could have 
tonight. Additionally, looks like the pressure gradient will be 
increasing as well, which should keep winds up a bit more and keep 
things better mixed compared to last night, and conceptually, keep 
things a bit warmer. If we do decouple and don't get the 
clouds...certainly could be as cold or colder than last night. Think 
the best shot at this occurring would be across NE Lower and the 
EUP, perhaps even as far west as the US-131 corridor, and will opt 
for a frost advisory tonight given lower confidence in temperatures 
tanking too far below 32F.  

Elevated Fire Danger Concerns Friday...Expect some dry/drier air to 
pivot in tonight/Friday morning from the east with increasing E/SE 
low-level flow. Some guidance is more aggressive bringing deeper 
moisture back into the area quicker Friday 
afternoon/evening...though given the antecedent dry air mass (RHs as 
of 18z today are just dropping below 30 percent in a few 
spots)...and guidance soundings suggesting we will be very dry in 
the lower levels, think we will stay drier longer than guidance 
suggests. Current expectation is for widespread afternoon RHs, 
especially away from Lake Huron, to drop into the 20-30 percent 
range, though certainly not out of the question it could get drier 
across NW Lower, where east-flow downsloping will certainly be in 
play. Potential sticky wicket with RHs will be high temps, as 
increasing mid-level cloud cover from the south could certainly put 
a damper on things...that is, if it is able to stick around without 
drying up as it reaches us. Additional concern with fire danger is 
potential for breezy/gusty east to southeast winds Friday...with 
pressure gradient supportive of sustained winds 10-20kts and high 
confidence in a period of gusts 15-25kts across the area...which 
would further cause issues with fire behavior. 

Rain Chances Friday night into Saturday...Think we have a decent 
shot at rain holding off till at least after sunset Friday, if not 
longer...given aforementioned concerns about dry low-levels, though
